MUSIC ACTIVITIES LESSON PLAN
 Week: Lesson:
 SCHOOL GRADE DATE TIME ROLL
 Two
STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: PERFORMING
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: SONGS: Types of Songs
Specific lesson learning outcome
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:-
 a) Identify different types of songs performed for different purposes to enhance comprehension.
 b) Sing a variety of age appropriate songs in unison paying attention to accuracy in pitch and rhythm for
 enjoyment.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
 1. During which activities do you sing?
 2. What do the songs that you sing talk about?

LEARNING RESOURCES:
  Recordings of different types of songs.
  ICT devices.
  KLB Visionary Music Activities Grade 2 Teachers guide pg. 2-4.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in groups and individually.
INTRODUCTION
Learners to sing a familiar song of their choice.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Play a recording of different types of songs for listening and guide learners to talk about the occasions
 when the songs are performed and the message they contain.
 Step 2: Guide the learners to identify the different types of songs according to purpose/message, style of
 performance and occasion when they are performed.e.g lullabies, story songs, and sacred songs.
 Step 3: Guide the learners to sing relevant familiar songs to illustrate the type of song and the message
 contained in the song. E.g. Lullaby “u kira mwana”.
 Step 4: Learners to act out and role play the content of songs as they sing.e.g “crossing the road”.
SUMMARY
Summarize the lesson by learners asking questions.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Close the lesson through singing age appropriate songs and paying attention to pitch and rhythm.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
 Learners to listen to different types of songs and identify the various types of songs.

ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Group/individual work.
INTRODUCTION
Guide learners to sing a familiar song to prepare them for singing lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Guide the learners to sing a two- part round e.g. “Mama Mbe Tsimbindi” following the steps below
 Sing the song in unison as a whole class
 Group the class into two
 Each group to sing in unison to ascertain that they know the song well
 Conduct the round, where one group starts the song and the other one begins to sing after the
 first phrase
 Step 2: Discuss with the learners the need to practice regularly and keeping time for rehearsals.
Step 3: Guide the learners to sing a second song e.g. “We come from many places” as a round
SUMMARY:
Summarize the lesson by asking learners to sing a 2-part rounds drawn from the local culture.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to listen to melodic flow of rounds so as to lean to sing the round song by imitation.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to sing round in two parts in well-coordinated groups.

STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: PERFORMING
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Kenya National Anthem
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to sing verse 1 and 2 of the Kenya National Anthem in
Kiswahili and English with proper etiquette to enhance patriotism, cohesion and peaceful co-existence.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
 1. When is Kenya national anthem performed?
 2. What do we learn in verse 1 of the Kenya national anthem?
 3. What do we learn in verse 2 of the Kenya national anthem?

  Pictures of some occasions when the anthem is performed
  ICT devices and recordings of the anthem
  KLB Visionary Music Activities Grade 2 Teachers guide pg. 6-9
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Group/individual work
INTRODUCTION
Guide the learners to sing a familiar song for warm up.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Conduct a discussion on the meaning of the words of the national anthem in relation to patriotism,
 cohesion and peaceful co-existence in 2nd verse
 Step 2: Guide the learners to recite the words of the 2nd verse in English and or Kiswahili
 Step 3: Teach the 2nd verse phrase by phrase and guide the learners to sing verse two as a whole.
 Step 4: Guide the learners to sing verse one and two in English and o Kiswahili while following etiquette by
 standing at attention, removing unofficial caps and showing respect for the country.
 SUMMARY
Summarize the lesson by asking the learners to sing the national anthem in groups.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Guide the learners to sing verse 2 o the anthem in both Kiswahili and English
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to listen to melody and text of Kenya national anthem and to imitate by singing.

SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Elements of music and vocal techniques
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:-
 a) Sing different songs while observing the elements of music as a basis of musicianship.
 b) Use different vocal techniques while singing for effective communication.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
 1. What elements of music would you apply in singing?
 2. What vocal techniques would you use for effective communication?

ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work I groups and individually.
INTRODUCTION
Guide the learners to sing a familiar song.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Guide the learners to identify the basic elements of music to be effected in singing; pitch, tempo,
 dynamics and rhythm.
 Step 2: Guide them to sing familiar songs, talk about where the elements can be applied and with what effect.
 Step 3: Learners to sing the songs in pairs, in groups and as a class applying the elements e.g. Miti
 yayumbayumba
 Step 4: Use the same song or other suitable songs to guide learners to identify vocal techniques to be used in
 singing for effective communication.
SUMMARY:
 Summarize the lesson by asking learners to name other techniques used in singing for effective
 communication.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
 Use suitable songs for learners to develop vocal techniques.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
 Learners to listen and to identify and to apply various elements of music and vocal techniques while singing
 either at school or at home.

 b) Sing familiar songs with body movements for self-expression.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
 1. What songs do you like to sing?
 2. What do you learn from the song?
 3. What do you feel when you sing them?

ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING

INTRODUCTION
Guide the learners to sing familiar songs to draw the attention to the messages in the songs.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Play a recording of selected presentations for learners to listen to or watch and guide learners to
 identify the expressions of ideas, feelings and emotions.
 Step 2: Guide them to know how expression of ideas, feelings and emotions are actualized through
 understanding the meaning of words, use of facial expressions, gestures and body movements.

Guide the learners to sing other familiar songs with facial expressions, gestures and body movements

The learner to listen and respond by singing songs at home and school while observing expression of ideas,
feelings and emotions.

SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Songs from diverse cultures
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to appreciate and enjoy singing songs from diverse cultures.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
 1. What do you like about songs sung in your language?
 2. What do you like about song sung in other languages?
 3. Why should we sing song in other languages?

INTRODUCTION
Ask the learners to sing a familiar song for warm up.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Guide the learners to appreciate and understand the messages in the songs from different cultures and

 Step 2: Play recorded songs from diverse cultural background for the learners to listen to and to talk about the

 Step 3: Guide the learner to sing some of the songs listened to and others sung in class e.g. lullabies.
 Step 4: Organize learners to sing the songs in pairs, small groups and then as the whole class.

Summarize the lesson by holding a discussion on the importance of preserving the original form of cultural
songs.

Learners to sing songs from other cultures that they are familiar with.

Learners to listen to different types of songs and the occasions when the songs are performed.

STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: PERFORMING
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Aspects of singing games
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to perform singing games from local and other cultures with
appropriate application of aspects of:-
 a) Singing for enjoyment.
 b) Movement for enjoyment.
 c) Props for enjoyment, and.
 d) Costumes for enjoyment.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
 1. How do you tell a good singer?
 2. How do you tell a good dancer?
 3. How are performers of singing games dressed?
 4. What materials or things are used while performing singing games?

ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Individual and group work.
INTRODUCTION
Learners to sing and dance to a familiar song .
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Guide the learners to identify the following aspects of singing: Rhythm, pitch, Diction, Soloist, Breath
 control, Tonality.
Step 2: Guide the learners to identify the following aspects of movement. Dancing in rhythm, making patterns,
being agile, and coordination of movement, choreography and patterns, good use of space.
Step 3: Guide the learners to identify different props in different singing games such as ropes, dolls, stones etc.
Step 4: Learners to appreciate the role of costumes by identifying costumes used by different performers
locally and from other cultures.
SUMMARY:
Learners to apply the aspects learnt while performing different appropriate singing games from their local and
other cultures e.g. “Mwana Mukhana”
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to singing familiar songs accompanied by the learnt aspects.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to performance various singing games in assistance with their friends.

 a) From local cultures for own safety.
 b) From other cultures for others, safety.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
 1. What injuries do children get while playing?
 2. What injuries can a child get while performing singing games?
 3. What should children do to avoid injuries while performing singing games?
